problemStatement.formal: For all n ≥ 2k the least prime factor of C(n,k) is ≤ max(n/k, k), with only finitely many exceptions.
problemStatement.plain: The least prime factor of binomial coefficients satisfies a simple bound with finitely many exceptions.
whyMatters: Connects prime factorization to binomial coefficients
Related to Selfridge's conjecture on n ≥ k²-1

proven: 12 of 14 known exceptions verified by native_decide
k=0 never exception, k=1 never exception (proved)
Bound simplification: when n≥k² reduces to lpf≤n/k, when n<k² reduces to lpf≤k
open: Main conjecture: finiteness of exception set
Selfridge's conjecture: holds for n ≥ k²-1 except C(62,6)
Strongest bound: lpf ≤ max(n/k, 13) with ≤12 exceptions
knownResults.goal: Verify exceptions computationally, prove structural properties

currentState.focus: Build: verify exceptions, prove k=0/k=1 cases, bound simplification
blockers: C(241,16) and C(284,28) too large for native_decide
currentState.nextAction: Aristotle submission, or try C(241,16) with longer timeout

knowledge.progressSummary: BUILD COMPLETED: 221-line formalization with 35 proved theorems, 0 sorries, 3 axioms. Verified 12/14 known exceptions computationally (C(241,16) and C(284,28) too large). Proved k=0 and k=1 never give exceptions, bound simplification properties, n=2k cases.
insights: minFac and choose are computable - native_decide handles most exceptions
C(241,16) and C(284,28) are too large for fast native_decide
The key difficulty is proving finiteness, not verifying specific exceptions
k=1 case follows from minFac(n) ≤ n and n/1 = n
Bound simplification via max_eq_left/max_eq_right is clean
